name: Yeast Strain Classification with Plate Batch Effects (Cheveralls et al. 2026)
description: Spontaneous Raman spectra of desiccated yeast cells for strain classification under strong plate-level batch effects: 9 strains -- 3 Saccharomyces cerevisiae (BY4741 WT, YNL141/ADA1, YGL058/UBE2A) and 6 Schizosaccharomyces pombe (SP286 WT, ED666 WT, PDF1/PPT1, RAD6/UBE2A, DEA2/ADA1, ARSG) -- grown to OD600 of 5, pelleted, washed, smeared onto a stainless-steel plate stamped with a 96-well layout and desiccated for ~3 h. 785 nm excitation, Wasatch Photonics WP-785X-F13-R-IL fiber probe (93 mW at the sample plane), 5 s integration with 10 averages, 5x5 position grid per well, across 3 independent end-to-end replicate plates (2025-08-06, 2025-08-07, 2025-08-12): 75 spectra per strain, 675 in total (the 75 empty-well control spectra are excluded). 235.7-3,653.6 cm^-1 at 2,048 points (non-uniform grid; the paper's analysis used a 300-1,800 cm^-1 fingerprint region). group_ids are the 3 desiccation plates (the dates above; 225 spectra each = 9 strain wells x 25 co-located site spectra) -- the paper's batch unit, so a grouped 3-fold split is exactly leave-one-plate-out CV, its protocol. The finer (plate, well) structure is documented here but not exposed as groups: well-level grouping would let spectra from the held-out plate's other wells into training and hide the batch effect. Spectra are raw as deposited -- no dark subtraction, baseline correction, or normalization; the per-plate dark spectra are in the archive (dark/Default.csv) for anyone replicating the authors' pipeline (ramanspy: Whitaker-Hayes despiking, consensus dark subtraction, low-intensity QC at mean < 1000, Savitzky-Golay, ModPoly order 5, AUC normalization, per-well outlier QC; leaves 24-33 spectra per strain). The paper shows standard 5-fold CV overestimates strain accuracy (median MCC 0.79) while leave-one-plate-out CV exposes the batch effect (median MCC 0.32), making this a purpose-built probe of group-aware cross-validation.

rai:dataCollectionType: Laboratory measurements on biological materials including microorganisms, cell cultures, fermentation broths, and plant material.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Spectra are provided with class labels. Any preprocessing applied (baseline correction, smoothing, normalisation) is described in the source publication.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Class labels assigned based on known sample identity or validated analytical reference methods.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All spectra originate from chemical, biological, or material samples without individual human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Data were acquired under controlled laboratory conditions and may not generalise to field or clinical settings. rai:dataLimitations: Spectral signatures are process- and instrument-specific; calibration transfer to other setups requires additional validation.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables the development of rapid, inline bioprocess monitoring tools that can reduce waste, improve yield, and lower costs in biomanufacturing and biotechnology.
